title: Three-tier storage and broad latency claims exceed evidence
competing_evidence: Whitepaper claims hot Roaring, warm Arrow, cold Parquet, promotion/demotion, millisecond retrieval, sub-microsecond set operations, and MVCC query isolation. Core has set/Roaring in-memory snapshots and one committed 10M scenario; Arrow/Polars are result conversions, no warm/cold tiers or tier movement exist, and Phase 3 did not rerun the benchmark. Server proves SQLite atomic publication, not general MVCC isolation.
adversarial_conclusion: The conclusion presents an architectural target as a current platform-wide performance fact. Existing bitmap and benchmark work supports only a narrowly scoped reference result.
required_adjudication: Choose whether the whitepaper is describing target architecture or the pinned release; approve bounded benchmark wording and the meaning of MVCC/isolation.
next_evidence: Regenerate the committed benchmark from a clean frozen environment; add concurrent reader/refresh isolation probes; either implement Arrow/Parquet tiers or mark them future.

title: Grammar status count is stale and grammar acceptance is over-read
competing_evidence: The whitepaper says 27 implemented statement types and full expression grammar. The current top-level grammar has 22 statement alternatives, calls itself a non-normative-complete scaffold, and multiple accepted statements lower to UNKNOWN or fail execution.
adversarial_conclusion: A count of grammar alternatives is volatile and does not establish implemented language capability.
required_adjudication: Approve generated syntax-surface reporting and separate parse, lower, and execute maturity in public status tables.
next_evidence: Generate grammar production counts in CI and add a parse/lower/execute conformance matrix for every top-level statement.

title: Parser has no error recovery contract
competing_evidence: The whitepaper labels the parser 'with error recovery'; malformed first input raises ContextQLSyntaxError and prevents a later valid statement from being returned. Parser code normalizes one failure and re-raises; it has no synchronization/recovery loop.
adversarial_conclusion: The implemented parser has useful normalized diagnostics, not recovery.
required_adjudication: Decide whether recovery is required for files/editor workflows or whether the status claim should say error reporting only.
next_evidence: Add a recovery fixture containing malformed and later valid statements, or remove recovery wording.

title: Linter rule count is stale and coverage is incomplete
competing_evidence: The whitepaper says 11 rules; ContextQLLinter.lint invokes 12 rules. Many registered semantic/runtime codes are not linter rules and the catalog is in-memory.
adversarial_conclusion: The linter is implemented and tested, but a hand-maintained count is already wrong and can be mistaken for semantic completeness.
required_adjudication: Approve generated rule registry/status wording.
next_evidence: Derive the count and rule table from code; map each normative semantic rule to its actual emitter and tests.

title: Implemented table conflates symbol presence with complete public capability
evidence_ids: Core 554 passed/1 failed/1 skipped; Phase3 parse/lower/execute ladder
competing_evidence: Each named component exists, but important limits are hidden: unsupported statement kinds, incomplete scoring, no CLI watch/test commands, untested magics, no LSP live metadata/go-to-definition, one adapter, and no operational provider broker. Several cited paths are stale after providers became a package.
adversarial_conclusion: Most atomic existence claims are narrowly true, yet the undifferentiated 'Implemented' heading materially inflates end-to-end maturity.
required_adjudication: Adopt M-level or precise status labels in the whitepaper appendix and define what 'implemented' means for a component.
next_evidence: For each status row link executable contract tests and negative boundaries; correct stale paths and generate API/tooling inventories.

title: Type-system implementation is an unintegrated duplicate
competing_evidence: The whitepaper lists type-system definitions as implemented. contextql/types.py explicitly says integration is TODO; semantic.py defines a second EntityKeyType and executor validation is largely string/metadata based.
adversarial_conclusion: Types exist as a surface, but there is no single type authority or end-to-end type checker supporting the whitepaper's type-system claim.
required_adjudication: Choose the canonical type model and the v1 enforcement boundary.
next_evidence: Add type conformance fixtures from declarations through analyzer and executor; remove or integrate the duplicate module.

title: Standard SQL does not pass through unchanged
competing_evidence: The whitepaper twice promises unchanged standard SQL pass-through. SELECT 1 fails because FROM is required; all input must first satisfy the Lark subset and supported statements are reconstructed before DuckDB execution.
adversarial_conclusion: The pinned engine is SQL-like and DuckDB-backed, not transparent SQL:2016 pass-through.
required_adjudication: Approve an explicit dialect/conformance profile and compatibility policy.
next_evidence: Build positive and negative SQL conformance fixtures by feature/dialect; rewrite both claims to the measured subset.

title: Polars and Arrow are outputs, not execution targets
competing_evidence: Whitepaper says execution targets DuckDB, Polars, and Arrow. Only DuckDBAdapter executes queries; Polars and Arrow occur in Result conversion.
adversarial_conclusion: The current claim incorrectly promotes output interoperability to adapter execution support.
required_adjudication: Decide whether Polars/Arrow adapters remain planned or are removed from current architecture wording.
next_evidence: Add adapter contract tests for any claimed target; otherwise relabel them as optional result formats.

title: Score-range warning code conflicts across authorities
competing_evidence: Whitepaper assigns out-of-range score warning W100; SPEC and implementation assign W100 to stale snapshots and W003 to score range. DECISIONS requires a warning but does not reconcile the code collision.
adversarial_conclusion: Clients cannot rely on warning-code identity while three authorities assign different meanings.
required_adjudication: Design authority must establish a generated canonical code registry and explicit supersession entries.
next_evidence: Add tests that emit each warning from the public API and validate docs/spec against the registry.

title: Score domain and nullability are not enforced as claimed
competing_evidence: Whitepaper types CONTEXT_SCORE as [0,1] or NULL/unbounded only explicitly. Runtime weights and accumulation can exceed 1, missing scores become 0 or membership-derived 1, and the linter warning is heuristic rather than a type/domain guarantee.
adversarial_conclusion: The public score contract mixes recommended range, type domain, null behavior, and aggregation without executable normative rules.
required_adjudication: Settle normalization, null, negation, weighting, and aggregation semantics.
next_evidence: Create a score conformance suite covering out-of-range values, missing scores, negative/zero weights, multiple contexts, negation, and every strategy.

title: Temporal semantics directly conflict with executable membership history
competing_evidence: Whitepaper and older OQ-9 define temporal-column filtering; current SPEC/later decisions and executor replay membership history for AT/BETWEEN, while AT VERSION selects snapshot versions. BETWEEN uses ever-present membership and max observed score.
adversarial_conclusion: This is not editorial drift: the same syntax has incompatible meanings and can change result membership.
required_adjudication: Record explicit supersession and choose one meaning or distinct syntax for event-time filtering versus membership-history queries.
next_evidence: Add normative fixtures with the same rows producing different outcomes under the two models, including retention boundaries and BETWEEN score behavior.

title: CONTEXT_SCORE scope error code is wrong in the whitepaper
competing_evidence: Whitepaper says E111; implementation/README use E108 for scope and reserve E111 for score-expression type errors.
adversarial_conclusion: A documented stable diagnostic is assigned to two meanings.
required_adjudication: Approve E108 or a replacement via the canonical registry and mark the other statement superseded.
next_evidence: Add a documentation-registry consistency check and public negative test.

title: Window-without-score warning code and behavior conflict
competing_evidence: Whitepaper uses W101 and promises entity-key ascending truncation; implementation uses W001 while W101 means failed refresh. Tooling hover says scores are required, conflicting with warning-and-continue behavior.
adversarial_conclusion: Both code identity and legality are inconsistent; deterministic runtime ordering lacks a focused executor fixture.
required_adjudication: Choose legal-with-warning versus invalid and define unscored ordering.
next_evidence: Add end-to-end window fixtures on deliberately unsorted keys and synchronize hover/spec/error registry.

title: DEVIATION_SCORE is documented as executable semantics without a runtime
competing_evidence: Whitepaper specifies DEVIATION_SCORE range, but event logs and process models do not execute and no process-function runtime establishes the value.
adversarial_conclusion: A return-domain claim cannot be verified before the function and its model execution exist.
required_adjudication: Confirm whether process intelligence is normative v1, reference design, or future research.
next_evidence: Implement a minimal event-log/process-model vertical slice with conformance fixtures or mark all process return contracts non-current.

title: OCEL future status is internally sound but forward-compatibility is unproved
competing_evidence: Whitepaper/decisions consistently defer OCEL, but also claim current CREATE EVENT LOG is forward-compatible. The DDL is parse/model-only and no OCEL evolution/migration fixture demonstrates compatibility.
adversarial_conclusion: The deferral is correctly labeled; the stronger compatibility assurance is speculative.
required_adjudication: Retain OCEL as future and decide whether forward-compatible is a requirement or aspiration.
next_evidence: Define an OCEL extension sketch and prove current identifiers/catalog shapes can migrate without semantic break, or soften the claim.

title: Nine-state lifecycle is not implemented or enforced
evidence_ids: Focused core probe: retired context remained queryable
competing_evidence: Whitepaper promises a governed nine-state FSM and production guarantees. Core accepts four strings, CREATE sets active, server immediately rewrites create to draft, and query execution does not gate retired/draft contexts.
adversarial_conclusion: Lifecycle is catalog metadata plus a few server endpoints, not the claimed state machine or query-safety boundary.
required_adjudication: Choose canonical states, legal transitions, core/server create semantics, and query visibility rules.
next_evidence: Add state-transition matrices, invalid-transition tests, restart tests, and query probes in every state before asserting governance.

title: Freshness codes and refresh behavior are internally inconsistent
evidence_ids: Core errors.py registry; server scheduler tests
competing_evidence: Whitepaper uses W010/W012/W013, max_staleness, async/sync refresh policy, and dependency-version warnings. Implementation uses stale_after with W100, refresh-failure W101, an optional polling scheduler, and has no W013 emitter or strict_freshness behavior.
adversarial_conclusion: Freshness behavior is a mix of incompatible vocabulary, codes, and unimplemented policy branches.
required_adjudication: Adopt one freshness model and specify whether stale reads trigger work, block, or only warn.
next_evidence: Create clock-controlled stale/very-stale/failed-refresh/dependency-version tests across core and restart-persistent server state.

title: v1 micro-batch streaming claims contradict explicit deferral and code
evidence_ids: Static decisions OPS-3; no embedded generic micro-batch processor found
competing_evidence: Whitepaper claims v1 embedded one-second micro-batching and compares it as a current alternative, while its own status/future sections and DECISIONS defer streaming. The DeepSee synchronizer folds a connector change feed but is not a generic streaming processor.
adversarial_conclusion: Current-tense v1 streaming claims are false for the pinned pair and conflict with explicit deferral.
required_adjudication: Confirm deferral and distinguish connector incremental synchronization from generic streaming semantics.
next_evidence: Remove/currently-label v1 statements; define a future minimal slice, delivery owner, watermark/replay contract, and load/failure experiment.

title: Future capabilities are correctly labeled but detailed prose risks implied commitment
competing_evidence: LLM synthesis, multi-adapter/distributed execution, external streaming, and temporal identity are explicitly future/deferred, but surrounding sections describe concrete APIs/architecture in present tense.
adversarial_conclusion: These two high-risk claims are not implementation gaps when retained as non-committed future directions; the risk is status leakage from detailed design prose.
required_adjudication: Approve whether each is committed, incubating, or illustrative, with a target maturity and sponsor only if committed.
next_evidence: Keep future sections visually separate; add roadmap decision state and a falsifiable experiment for any item promoted beyond research.

title: Production-ready security and compliance claims are unsafe
evidence_ids: Server 109 tests pass, but no auth/RBAC/RLS/tenant abuse suite exists
competing_evidence: Whitepaper claims fail-closed privileges, RLS/classification propagation, hash-chained Parquet audit, tenant isolation, and regulated-industry readiness. Core only parses GRANT and emits callbacks; server has unauthenticated routes and mutable SQLite audit rows without hash chain or authorization.
adversarial_conclusion: This is the most dangerous maturity inflation: public claims describe controls that are absent at enforcement boundaries.
required_adjudication: Immediately classify security prose as reference design, remove production-ready/compliance assurance, and assign a human security design authority before implementation claims resume.
next_evidence: Threat model; route authorization tests; tenant-isolation abuse tests; RLS fixtures; credential-boundary review; tamper-evident audit verification; independent security review.

title: Server explain is an executing endpoint, not a plan endpoint
competing_evidence: Whitepaper defines POST /v1/query/explain as returning an execution plan; actual unversioned /query/explain invokes normal execution and returns rows plus trace. Core Engine.explain is dry, so identically named surfaces have opposite safety properties.
adversarial_conclusion: Callers can cause provider calls, data reads, or future mutations while expecting plan-only behavior.
required_adjudication: Decide whether server explain must be dry. If execution/trace is desired, give it a distinct explicit endpoint and authorization policy.
next_evidence: Add no-execution spies for adapter/provider/DDL paths, authorization tests, and OpenAPI side-effect documentation.

title: Persistent provider registry is not a runtime broker
competing_evidence: Server CRUD persists provider metadata and stored health, but startup does not instantiate or register persisted providers with core. Health returns stored state rather than an active endpoint probe. Built-in/mock providers are wired separately.
adversarial_conclusion: A configured provider can appear enabled/healthy in control-plane metadata yet be unavailable to query execution.
required_adjudication: Define provider factory/credential resolution, activation lifecycle, health semantics, and failure policy.
next_evidence: Restart an externally configured provider and query it end to end; inject bad credentials, timeout, schema mismatch, and disabled-state cases.

title: Identity registry is not the global confidence-based identity model
competing_evidence: Whitepaper says mappings link system-specific keys to canonical global IDs with confidence. Runtime synchronization sends exact table.column path pairs; confidence/matching mode are stored metadata and no canonical entity records or probabilistic resolver exist.
adversarial_conclusion: The implemented feature is deterministic column binding, materially narrower than identity resolution.
required_adjudication: Rename/reframe the current feature or approve a canonical identity model with confidence semantics and governance.
next_evidence: Cross-system key-type tests, ambiguity/confidence fixtures, provenance, lifecycle, privacy, and authorization tests.

title: Server version identity is contradictory
competing_evidence: Generated OpenAPI/application startup reports 0.3.0; installed package metadata and README report 0.1.0; core reports 0.2.0.
adversarial_conclusion: Clients and audit records cannot identify a coherent server release or compatible pair.
required_adjudication: Choose the authoritative server version and publish a core/server compatibility matrix.
next_evidence: CI assertion across package metadata, FastAPI OpenAPI, startup audit, README, and release tag.

title: Public context-update fields are accepted but ignored
competing_evidence: ContextUpdate accepts entity_key, has_score, and classification, but CatalogService.update applies definition, description, tags, and score-column changes only.
adversarial_conclusion: A successful request may silently fail to apply user intent, which is worse than explicit rejection for catalog semantics.
required_adjudication: Decide which fields are mutable and their compatibility/version consequences.
next_evidence: One contract test per request field asserting persisted and engine-observed behavior; reject unsupported fields with a stable error.

title: Multi-statement parsing is not multi-statement execution
competing_evidence: Parser/lowerer retain two statements, but Engine.execute returns only the first result and silently ignores the second. CLI file mode implements separate naive splitting.
adversarial_conclusion: Silent truncation can omit DDL or queries without an error and has no explicit public contract.
required_adjudication: Choose reject-extras, execute transactionally, or return a multi-result type.
next_evidence: Probe SELECT+DDL and DDL+failing-DDL atomicity; add semicolon-in-literal CLI fixtures.

title: Composite and native parameter syntax stop before execution
evidence_ids: Focused core probe: COMPOSE query failed Unknown context
competing_evidence: COMPOSE models and dependencies persist, but no live resolution or composite snapshot is built. Native context parameter declarations/invocations lower, but arguments are not validated/substituted; only MCP receives parameters.
adversarial_conclusion: These are parse/model surfaces that look like core language features but lack end-to-end semantics.
required_adjudication: Approve v1 semantics for composition strategy/scoring and native parameter binding, or explicitly mark both designed.
next_evidence: Successful and negative create/query/refresh/restart tests for each strategy and parameter type/default/error case.

title: THEN currently collapses to intersection
competing_evidence: Whitepaper describes candidate-scoped staged, left-associative evaluation; executor combines masks with AND and explicitly notes staged scoping is not enforced. The Phase 3 result is indistinguishable from intersection.
adversarial_conclusion: The same syntax cannot safely stand for staged retrieval, temporal sequence, and set intersection.
required_adjudication: Choose one normative meaning or introduce distinct operators.
next_evidence: Use an instrumented provider whose second-stage result/call depends on the candidate set; test associativity, scores, side effects, and failures.

title: Advertised score strategies are not strategy-specific execution
competing_evidence: Grammar accepts MAX, MIN, AVG, SUM, COUNT, WEIGHTED_MAX, WEIGHTED_SUM; executor performs fixed accumulation/intersection behavior and does not switch on all strategy values.
adversarial_conclusion: Parsing an ORDER BY strategy currently overstates executable score algebra.
required_adjudication: Resolve default and per-strategy formulas, normalization, negation, and tie-breaking.
next_evidence: Golden result matrix for each strategy across union/intersection, missing scores, multiple bindings, weights, ties, and snapshots.

title: Event/process/security/provider DDL is mostly parse-only
competing_evidence: EXPLAIN CONTEXT and provider/security/settings DDL lower to UNKNOWN; event/process CREATE lower but do not execute; companion event/process DDL is also unsupported.
adversarial_conclusion: The grammar creates a broad apparent language whose executable subset is much smaller.
required_adjudication: Approve which statements are normative v1 versus reserved syntax.
next_evidence: Machine-generated statement ladder requiring parse, model, analyzer, executor, errors, and persistence evidence before public status elevation.

title: Full core suite is import-order-sensitive
competing_evidence: Frozen core collected 556 tests: 554 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped. The Polars test infers package absence from sys.modules and passes on a targeted rerun only when imported first.
adversarial_conclusion: The product conversion works, but clean-suite green status is nondeterministic and cannot be claimed without qualification.
required_adjudication: Treat optional-dependency presence via import discovery, not import order.
next_evidence: Repair the test and rerun the entire frozen suite in clean environments with and without each optional extra.

title: HTTP surface is unversioned, under-documented, and ahead of package metadata
competing_evidence: OpenAPI exposes 27 unversioned operations while whitepaper examples use /v1 and server README describes mainly health/query. Current surface includes durable catalog, refresh, history, provider, identity, audit, and explain operations.
adversarial_conclusion: The product has evolved beyond its README but without an explicit API version/compatibility contract.
required_adjudication: Choose route versioning and stability policy before describing these endpoints as public.
next_evidence: Commit generated OpenAPI; run compatibility diff in CI; add README examples for every supported public route and deprecation rules.
